newsitem.title: CHINA: China ethylene plant output exceeds capacity.
newsitem.headline: China ethylene plant output exceeds capacity.

text.p: Dushanzi Petrochemical Plant in China's northwestern Xinjiang region produced 153,000 tonnes of ethylene between July 1, 1996, and the end of May this year -- far above its official capacity, officials said on Wednesday.
Asked how the plant had been able to produce so much more than its official annual capacity of 140,000 tonnes, one plant official said the success was due to effective leadership.
"We managed (things) well," the Dushanzi official said by telephone from Xinjiang.

The 4.27 billion yuan ($500 million) ethylene plant generated 1.69 billion yuan in output value in the 11 months after formally starting full production on July 1, 1996, he said. Dushanzi Petrochemical Plant began ethylene production in November, 1995 and the plant had annual capacity of 120,000 tonnes last year, the official said. He gave no details of actual output.

The plant was expected to produce more than 160,000 tonnes of ethylene in the year to the end of June, the China News Service quoted petrochemical plant manager Chen Zongyu as saying, but gave no further details.
